title: EC2 Auto Scaling & Elastic Load Balancing
summary: Scale EC2 fleets on demand and spread traffic across healthy instances.
tldr: An **Auto Scaling group** (ASG) across several AZs replaces failed instances and adds or removes capacity. Even `min = max = 1` gives a single instance automatic recovery across AZs.

Scale on the right signal: **target tracking** on CPU or `ALBRequestCountPerTarget`, **backlog per instance** for SQS workers, **predictive scaling** for repeating daily patterns, **warm pools** for slow boots.
To scale horizontally the tier must be **stateless**: sessions in ElastiCache or DynamoDB, files in S3 or EFS, not on the instance.

keyFacts.text: ASGs use EC2 status checks by default. Turn on **ELB health checks** so instances whose app hangs are replaced, not just removed from the target group.
The **health check grace period** must exceed boot time, or the ASG kills instances that are still starting and loops forever.
The target group **deregistration delay** (connection draining) lets in-flight requests finish. Set it longer than your slowest request.
A **termination lifecycle hook** pauses an instance in `Terminating:Wait` so a script can copy logs or drain work before it's terminated.
New AMI → new **launch template version** → **instance refresh** with a minimum healthy percentage and checkpoints. That's immutable, zero-downtime rollout.

keywords.cue: single licensed instance must recover from AZ failure
hung app instance removed from ALB but never replaced
keywords.answer: Enable ELB health checks on the ASG

keywords.cue: new instances terminated in a loop during long bootstrap
capacity ready before the 08:00 spike every weekday
12-minute startup, unpredictable spikes, low idle cost
new instances overwhelmed while warming caches
copy logs before scale-in terminates an instance

users logged out when instances are replaced
keywords.answer: External session store (ElastiCache or DynamoDB), drop sticky sessions

keywords.cue: roll out a new AMI with no downtime
keywords.answer: New launch template version and instance refresh

keywords.cue: customer firewall needs fixed IPs but keep ALB routing
keywords.answer: NLB with Elastic IPs in front of the ALB (ALB-type target group)

traps: Sticky sessions don't make a tier stateless. Users are still lost when their instance goes away, and load stays uneven.
Scheduled scaling needs manual upkeep; when the pattern repeats but drifts, predictive scaling is the low-overhead answer.
CPU-based scaling fails for I/O-bound apps. Scale on request count per target instead.
An ALB has no static IPs. Use an NLB with Elastic IPs (or Global Accelerator) when fixed addresses are required.
A Spot fleet of one instance type in one AZ with lowest-price allocation maximizes interruptions; diversify and use price-capacity-optimized.
